_strings.@@32a1ae57414a: Treaty conformity — NM conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NM income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NM return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NM's resident return (PIT-1) starts from federal adjusted gross income: "LINE 9. Federal Adjusted Gross Income — Enter the federal adjusted gross income as reported on your federal Form 1040 or 1040SR, line 11" (2023 PIT-1 instructions, p. PIT-1-23). Income exempt from federal tax under a US tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through to NM. NM's additions to federal AGI are enumerated exclusively on Schedule PIT-ADJ lines 1-5: (1) interest/dividends from federal tax-exempt bonds, (2) federal net operating loss carryover, (3) refunded NM Section 529 contributions, (4) charitable land-donation deduction tied to the NM land conservation credit, and (5) tax paid by a pass-through entity. None of these is an add-back of federally tax-treaty-exempt income, foreign treaty income, or any income exempt under a US tax treaty (the word "treaty" does not appear in the PIT-1, PIT-B, or PIT-ADJ instructions). Because there is no treaty add-back, federally treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by New Mexico -> conforms.
_strings.@@437f3a12af29: New Mexico Child Day Care Credit — A New Mexico resident who (a) provided over half the cost of maintaining a household for one or more qualifying dependents, (b) was gainfully employed during the period claimed, (c) was not receiving TANF/New Mexico Works or similar public assistance during that period, and (d) paid unreimbursed, uncompensated child day care expenses. Use the PIT-Childcare worksheet and Form PIT-CG (caregiver statement).

_strings.@@a0a5cdee0c2a: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW refundable credit first available for tax year 2023 — the New Mexico Child Income Tax Credit, enacted by HB 144 (2023 Regular Session) amending Section 7-2-18.34 NMSA 1978 and available for taxable years beginning January 1, 2023. It is claimed by a New Mexico resident who is not a dependent of another individual, for each qualifying child as defined under the federal Internal Revenue Code, and steps down by adjusted gross income: $0-$25,000 = $600; over $25,000 to $50,000 = $400; over $50,000 to $75,000 = $200; over $75,000 to $100,000 = $100; over $100,000 to $200,000 = $75; over $200,000 to $350,000 = $50; over $350,000 = $25. state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form PIT-1, line 18: 'New Mexico Tax' with line 18a Rate Table Indicator ('R = Rate tables'). 2023 PIT-1 instructions, LINE 18: 'Unless you qualify for Schedule CC, calculate your New Mexico tax by using one of these methods and then complete line 18a: If you have income from sources inside and outside New Mexico, use your entry on PIT-B, line 14 or; Use the rate tables from the PIT-1 instructions, starting on page 1T.' Applied to line 17 New Mexico Taxable Income ('Add lines 9, 10, and 11, then subtract lines 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16. If the result is negative, enter zero.'). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply Form PIT-1, line 17 (New Mexico Taxable Income) = lines 9 (federal AGI) + 10 (SALT add-back for itemizers) + 11 (PIT-ADJ additions) MINUS lines 12-16, zero floor. Every deduction/exemption is computed ON THE FORM, so none ship as keys: line 12 is the filer's OWN federal standard or itemized deduction amount (whatever was allowable on federal Form 1040 line 12); line 13 is the $4,000 'Deduction for Certain Dependents' (HoH or MFJ filers only, and the worksheet multiplies $4,000 by total dependents MINUS ONE — do not model it as a flat per-dependent amount); line 14 is the New Mexico low- and middle-income tax exemption (up to $2,500 per federal exemption, phasing with AGI and filing status); line 15 is PIT-ADJ deductions/exemptions; line 16 the medical care expense deduction. Do NOT supply raw federal AGI. Adjudication note (two-pass): pass 1 = the 2023 PIT-TRT look-up table and its printed continuation schedules; pass 2 = the statutory Section 7-2-7 NMSA 1978 schedules (2019 HB 6, in force for 2021+, unchanged for 2023). The statutory 'plus' constants are EXACT cumulative sums ($93.50/$269.50/$504.50/$10,010.50 single; $136/$392/$768/$15,027 HoH-QSS-MFJ; $68/$196/$384/$7,513.50 MFS), so this engine's marginal accumulation reproduces the statute to the cent. CRITICAL — the filed line 18 value comes from the MANDATED look-up table, which sits a few dollars BELOW statutory marginal math: for line 17 of $96,000 or less the TRT table row (in $100 bands, computed at band midpoints) is the filed figure; over $96,000 the TRT continuation schedule CHAINS FROM THE LAST TABLE ROW ('Your Tax is $4,422 + 4.9% of excess over $96,000' single; $4,294 MFJ/HoH; $4,498 MFS) instead of the statutory cumulative ($4,424.50 / $4,296 / $4,500), so the filed figure runs about $2-$3 below this engine's statutory bracket math at high incomes (TRT top-tier constants $10,008/$15,025/$7,512 vs statutory $10,010.50/$15,027/$7,513.50). The filed form must take the table/schedule value — never plain bracket arithmetic (the NM hand-fill pack's line 18 carries the same mandate). Statuses: the statute groups 'heads of household, surviving spouses and married individuals filing joint returns' on ONE schedule — head_of_household here is the SAME schedule as married_filing_jointly (copied per the schema, not derived), and the TRT prints identical MFJ and HoH columns with the footnote '* This column must also be used by surviving spouse', so qualifying surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly exactly as the engine assumes. The single schedule also applies to estates and trusts (Section 7-2-7(C) NMSA 1978: 'For single individuals and for estates and trusts'). Not modeled on the same return: line 19 additional tax on lump-sum distributions (NM's 5x averaging method, Line 19 worksheet); PIT-B allocation/apportionment for income from sources inside and outside New Mexico (line 18 then comes from PIT-B line 14, indicator B); line 20 credit for taxes paid to another state; PIT-CR business credits; and the refundable credits/rebates (Working Families Tax Credit 25% of the federal EIC, Child Income Tax Credit, PIT-RC rebates) — all tax credits or separate computations, never base reductions. New Mexico has no state-defined standard deduction or personal exemption of its own — the federal deduction flows through on line 12 (federal Form 1040 line 12 amount), which is why the caller supplies the form's own taxable-income line.
